empty.title: Nothing imported yet
empty.body: After your first import, this page shows:
empty.history: Import history: every file you imported, what it added, and a way to undo it.
empty.formats: Saved formats: how each bank's file is read, so the next one needs no setup.
empty.identifiers: Account numbers and names: what your files call each account, so the right one is suggested.

history.title: Import history
history.description: Every file you imported, newest first. Undoing an import removes the transactions it added.
history.empty: No imports yet. Each file you import is listed here with what it added, and can be undone.
history.undone: The import of {{file}} was undone. Transactions removed: {{count}}.
history.undoneScanFailed: The import was undone, but subscriptions could not be checked again. Open Subscriptions and choose Rescan.

undo.title: Undo this import?
undo.loading: Working out what this import added…
undo.intro: Undoing removes everything this import added:
undo.edited: Changed by you since the import
undo.editedWarning: Categories, notes and other changes you made to these transactions after the import will be lost.
undo.transferNote: The other side of each transfer stays. It goes back to income or expense, unless you set its type yourself.
undo.afterwards: Loan balances and subscriptions are worked out again afterwards.
undo.irreversible: This cannot be reversed. To get the transactions back, import the file again.
undo.impactFailed: Could not work out what this import added, so it cannot be undone right now.

errors.generic: The import could not be undone. Try again; if it keeps failing, the Developer Console in Settings shows what went wrong.
errors.notReady: The database is still starting. Try again in a moment.
errors.IMPORT_BATCH_NOT_FOUND: This import is no longer in the history. It may already have been undone, for example in another tab.

formats.title: Saved formats
formats.description: How each bank's file is read, saved per account. A file in a format saved for its account skips the setup steps.
formats.empty: No saved formats yet. When an import remembers how a file is laid out, the format is kept here, so the next file from that bank needs no setup.

editDialog.title: Edit saved format
editDialog.name: Format name
editDialog.nameRequired: Enter a name for this format.
editDialog.accountHelp: Files in this format skip the setup steps for this account. For another account, the import checks how to read them first.
editDialog.saveFailed: The format could not be saved. Try again.

deleteDialog.title: Delete this saved format?
deleteDialog.body: "{{name}}" will be forgotten. The next time you import a file like this, the import will ask how to read it again.
deleteDialog.note: Transactions you already imported are not affected.
deleteDialog.failed: The format could not be deleted. Try again.

identifiers.title: Account numbers and names
identifiers.description: What your bank's files call each account. The import uses these to work out which account a file belongs to.
identifiers.empty: Nothing remembered yet. When you confirm which account a file belongs to, the number or name the file uses is kept here.
identifiers.label: Name in the file: "{{text}}"
identifiers.cardsNote: Card numbers are kept with each account on the Accounts page.

removeDialog.title: Remove from {{account}}?
removeDialog.body: {{identifier}} will no longer point to {{account}}. The next file that uses it will ask which account it belongs to.
removeDialog.failed: It could not be removed. Try again.
